prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a side impact at intersection in Katy, Texas, and has shoulder injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1455; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement is about the collision at the intersection in Katy, Texas. Do you understand that this call is being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Can you describe where you were driving and what you were doing just before the collision?

A: I was heading east on the main road toward the shopping center. The light had been green for a little while, and I was going the speed limit, maybe a bit under.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before impact?

A: Not really. It came through from the cross street on my right. I think it had been stopped at the sign. I braked, but there wasn't time to avoid it.

Q: Where did the vehicles make contact?

A: On my driver's side, just behind the front door. The airbag on my side went off, and my car spun a little before it stopped.

Q: Were you taken for medical attention?

A: An ambulance took me to the emergency room. They X-rayed my shoulder and neck and said I had a strain and some bruising. The shoulder is the main problem. It hurts when I lift my arm above my head, and I can't sleep on that side.

Q: Are you currently under the care of a doctor for the shoulder?

A: Yes, I have a follow-up with an orthopedic specialist next week. They mentioned physical therapy might be needed.

Q: Have you had any prior injuries to that shoulder?

A: No, nothing that required treatment. I play some recreational tennis, but I hadn't had any problems before this.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you think I should know about the accident?

A: I just want to make sure you have the photos I took at the scene. The other driver said they were sorry, and I gave my information to the police officer who responded.

Q: That's helpful. Thank you for your cooperation today.
